sections.label: Merger of IE and SPRING
sections.summary: The Enterprise Singapore Board Bill creates Enterprise Singapore, replacing the IE Singapore and SPRING Singapore Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In September 2017, I announced the Ministry of Trade and Industry’s (MTI's) plan to merge International Enterprise (IE) Singapore and the Standards, Productivity and Innovation Board (SPRING) Singapore and form a new dedicated agency for enterprise development – Enterprise Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The Enterprise Singapore Board Bill will give effect to the new Statutory Board and replace the International Enterprise Singapore Board Act and the Standards, Productivity and Innovation Board Act.

sections.label: SPRING and IE support numbers
sections.summary: In 2017 SPRING Singapore supported close to 40,000 companies and IE supported more than 45,000 companies overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In 2017, SPRING Singapore supported the capability upgrading of close to 40,000 companies, almost three times the number supported in 2010.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Similarly, IE supported more than 45,000 companies in their overseas ventures last year, more than double the number supported five years ago.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore standards and accreditation
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore will build on SPRING Singapore's efforts to develop internationally-recognised standards and quality assurance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: As the national standards and accreditation body, Enterprise Singapore will build on SPRING Singapore's efforts to develop internationally-recognised standards and quality assurance, which have burnished Singapore's reputation for high-quality and trustworthy products and services.

sections.label: Wholesale trade and consumer protection transfer
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore leads the Wholesale Trade map, while SPRING's fair trading function moves to CCS, renamed CCCS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore will take over from IE as the lead agency for the Wholesale Trade Industry Transformation Map to build a vibrant ecosystem of wholesale traders supported by talent with the right skillsets for the industry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: SPRING Singapore's consumer protection fair trading function will be transferred to the Competition Commission of Singapore (CCS).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The new Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS) will oversee all regulations and enforcement pertaining to consumer protection and ensuring a well-functioning market for the benefit of businesses as well as consumers.

sections.label: Competition Act amendments and transfers
sections.summary: The Competition Act will be amended to add fair trading and consumer protection functions, with SPRING's related assets transferred to CCCS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In particular, the Competition Act will be amended to update CCS' statutory functions to include the promotion of fair trading, prevention of unfair practices among suppliers in Singapore, advising relevant organisations on consumer protection matters generally, and the enforcement of the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act (CPFTA).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, CCS will be renamed CCCS to reflect its new statutory consumer protection function.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This Part also provides for the transfer to the new CCCS of SPRING Singapore's assets, employees, liabilities and records relating to the fair trading functions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Just as companies must adapt to keep pace with changes in the global economy, Government agencies and their programmes must also respond with agility to the shifting needs of industries and enterprises.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: I am confident that with the merger of IE and SPRING Singapore and the integration of their operations to form Enterprise Singapore, we will be well-placed to work closely with all stakeholders to transform our industries and grow stronger Singapore companies and a vibrant enterprise ecosystem to seize growth opportunities in the future economy.

sections.label: Government restructuring examples
sections.summary: Recent government restructurings such as IMDA and JTC consolidation are cited, with the SPRING and IE merger as the next move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Indeed, we have recently seen notable restructuring efforts in the Government space, such as the merger of the Infocomm Development Authority (IDA) and the Media Development Authority (MDA) to form the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) and the consolidation of Housing and Development Board (HDB) industrial properties into JTC, among others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: With enterprise capability-building and internationalisation as among the two key thrusts in the current phase of transformation, the merger of SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore is the next logical move.

sections.label: Minister's assurance on Enterprise Singapore
sections.summary: Minister Iswaran assured the House that Enterprise Singapore will support enterprises regardless of size or stage of growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In his answer to my Parliamentary Question last year on the impact of the merger, Minister Iswaran assured the House that Enterprise Singapore will continue "to support our enterprises, regardless of their size or stage of growth".

sections.label: Industry Transformation Maps approach
sections.summary: The Industry Transformation Maps tap ecosystem partners' expertise and resources to build capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs), which tap on the collective expertise and resources of the ecosystem partners to build capabilities is the way to go.

sections.label: SME survey finance issues
sections.summary: In last year's DP Information Group SME Development Survey, over a third of SMEs cited finance-related issues as their immediate business challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In last year’s DP Information Group SME Development Survey, more than a third of SMEs surveyed also cited finance-related issues as their immediate business challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This has more than doubled, compared to the survey done in 2014.

sections.label: Support for clause 68(b) and Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports clause 68(b) transferring CPFTA administration to the renamed CCCS and supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: On the related amendment, I support clause 68(b) which transfers the functions relating to the administration of CPFTA to the renamed CCCS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I believed this would sharpen the focus and add more teeth in enforcing fair trading and, hence, better protect consumers, an area we clearly need to do more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: With that, Mr Deputy Speaker, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This merger will allow for an integrated support network for businesses to build capability and access to both local and overseas markets.

sections.label: Question on Enterprise Singapore organisation
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the new Enterprise Singapore will be organised and restructured to help companies transform, grow and go global.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop of change and the pace of change, can the Minister share how the new Enterprise Singapore will be organised and restructured to work with companies to be responsive to helping them, both large and small, transform, grow and go global?

sections.label: Question on assistance schemes and integration
sections.summary: The speaker asks how Enterprise Singapore will structure assistance schemes and eligibility criteria, and supports integrating SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With changing business models, instead of working alone, more companies will partner to deliver products or services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, can the Minister share how Enterprise Singapore will structure the various assistance schemes and eligibility criteria for these schemes in such circumstances?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With that, Mr Deputy Speaker, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The move to integrate the functions of SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore would facilitate the provision of domestic and international state support to enterprises in a coordinated fashion, in a manner of a one-stop shop.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore support approaches
sections.summary: Asks whether Enterprise Singapore will provide different approaches to support local enterprises based on their needs, abilities and aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will Enterprise Singapore, therefore, provide different approaches in this manner to support local enterprises based on their needs, abilities and aspirations?

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore role differentiation
sections.summary: Asks how Enterprise Singapore's role will be differentiated from other economic agencies like the EDB and STB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Fourthly, and relatedly, how will Enterprise Singapore's role be differentiated from that of other economic agencies like the EDB and STB?

sections.label: Workers' Party supports consolidation
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports consolidating local enterprise support under Enterprise Singapore, citing SMEs' smaller value-added share and the need to groom globally competitive local companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Workers’ Party supports this move to consolidate local enterprise support under Enterprise Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Right now, their share of value-added is much smaller than their share of jobs, implying that we need to move those capable and aspirational SMEs up the productivity ladder.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And at the apex, we need to groom a critical mass of local companies to become globally competitive, with the centre of gravity and critical headquarters functions rooted in Singapore.

sections.label: Validating grants before disbursement
sections.summary: States it is prudent that successful grant claims under both Statutory Boards be validated by an externally appointed auditing company before disbursement during the merger.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Indeed, it is prudent to ensure that while the merger is in execution, all successful claims for grants under both Statutory Boards before the merger would first be validated by an externally appointed auditing company before disbursement.

sections.label: Grants pre-approved before acquisition
sections.summary: Notes SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore will ensure all legitimate grants are pre-approved before the acquisition process, and hopes consolidated resources enable closer work with businesses.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This worried them as they felt that their plans would be hampered.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that both SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore will ensure all legitimate grants are pre-approved before implementing the acquisition process.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Following the merger, I hope that the consolidated resources will enable Enterprise Singapore to work more closely with businesses.

sections.label: Hopes for SME growth
sections.summary: Many are looking forward to whether the new merged entity can help SMEs grow and scale their business at home and overseas.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Many are looking forward to see if the new merged entity can help SMEs to grow and scale their business at home and overseas.

sections.label: Merger of IE and SPRING
sections.summary: The Bill provides the legislative basis for the official merger of IE Singapore and SPRING Singapore on 1 April.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, first, I would like to declare that I am the Vice-Chairman of the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) and the Immediate Past President of SCCCI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill provides the legislative basis for the official merger of IE Singapore and SPRING Singapore on 1 April.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore Board establishment
sections.summary: Eight years after the recommendation, the Enterprise Singapore Board is being established, with local companies' competitiveness ranking behind several economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, eight years after raising the recommendation, we are finally seeing the establishment of the Enterprise Singapore Board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When the World Economic Forum recently announced its 2017-2018 Global Competitiveness Report, Singapore came up third in the global ranking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, the competitiveness and capabilities of local companies, including SMEs, are not amongst the top three, ranking behind their counterparts in Switzerland, Germany, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Malaysia and other economies.

sections.label: Merger effect on local enterprises
sections.summary: The merger could create a "one plus one, greater than two" effect, helping local enterprises grow and creating quality jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As EDB attracts foreign investors, it could also provide opportunities for local enterprises to be part of the industry supply chain and collaborate with MNCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope that the merger of these two Government agencies could lead to a more effective operation, creating a “one plus one, greater than two” effect, helping local enterprises to grow, and creating even more quality job opportunities for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Our SMEs make up the majority of our enterprises, employ two-thirds of our workforce and contribute to about half of Singapore’s GDP.

sections.label: Consolidation for SME support
sections.summary: SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore consolidate to provide one-stop support to SMEs for growth, development and internationalisation needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Expanding our SMEs overseas will also give our working people more opportunities to gain international work experience and enhance job mobility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, timely that SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore consolidate to provide one-stop support to our SMEs for their growth, development and internationalisation needs.

sections.label: Employees affected by merger
sections.summary: A total of 960 employees will be affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: A total of 960 employees will be affected.

sections.label: IE Singapore overseas expansion help
sections.summary: In the first half of 2017, IE Singapore helped 24,000 enterprises with overseas expansion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: For example, in the first half of 2017, IE Singapore helped 24,000 enterprises with overseas expansion.

sections.label: SME Centres under Enterprise Singapore
sections.summary: The Government established SME Centres supervised by the new Enterprise Singapore to bring policies to companies' doorsteps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Government also established SME Centres under the supervision of the new Enterprise Singapore to bring policies to the doorsteps of companies.

sections.label: Companies with $500,000 share capital
sections.summary: All Singapore-registered companies with a share capital of $500,000 and above must join SBF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Today, all Singapore-registered companies with a share capital of $500,000 and above have to join SBF.

sections.label: SME Centres and Business Grant Portal
sections.summary: SME Centres spend much time bringing grants and schemes to over 200,000 companies yearly, but the Business Grant Portal lets savvy companies self-help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For now, SME Centres spend a large proportion of their time in bringing the Government grants and incentive schemes to companies, and they have been effective in reaching out to more than 200,000 companies annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, with the launch of the Business Grant Portal (BGP), companies here, especially those which are savvy, will be able to self-help for Government schemes.

sections.label: Singaporeans, business transformation, Enterprise Singapore
sections.summary: Many Singaporeans above 45 are anxious about business transformation, so mass communication should make them think differently, and Enterprise Singapore will catalyse ITM ownership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Many Singaporeans, especially those above 45 who consume these news channels, are deeply aware of the implication of the ongoing business transformation, because they live through it every day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And many of them have a deep anxiety about what is next and how to adjust to the changing world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, using the mass communication channel to talk about the fate of different industries will not just focus everybody on these industries, but getting everyday Singaporeans to think about how to do things differently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But all it means is trying to do things differently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, we must get as many Singaporeans who are staffing our SMEs, who are business owners, as possible to think about doing things differently all the time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I have full confidence that Enterprise Singapore will do a good job catalysing widespread and deep industry ownership of the ITMs and level up our companies.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore pooling resources
sections.summary: As a single agency, Enterprise Singapore can pool resources and expertise across a wider spectrum of corporate strategies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As a single agency, Enterprise Singapore will be able to pool together resources and expertise across a wider spectrum of corporate strategies.

sections.label: Streamlining SME form-filling procedures
sections.summary: The question asks whether the new entity's synergies will streamline or reduce form-filling procedures required by SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the synergies of the new entity, will the form-filling procedures, for example, required by SMEs be streamlined or reduced?

sections.label: IE Singapore initiatives for firms
sections.summary: IE Singapore initiatives like GCP and MRA should continue under Enterprise Singapore, and the Malay/Muslim business community identifies three areas for Government help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Current IE Singapore initiatives, such as the Global Company Partnership (GCP) grant and Market Readiness Assistance (MRA) should continue to be offered in some form by Enterprise Singapore as they will remain highly relevant to any firms’ strategy to internationalise their businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Malay/Muslim business community also believes that to stay competitive globally, there are three top areas that the Government could help them improve on.

sections.label: QBE survey on SME internationalisation
sections.summary: A QBE Insurance survey found only 14% of SMEs intend to expand overseas while 45% have no plans, citing funding, unfamiliarity and competition concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As the Minister would be aware, a recent survey by QBE Insurance that was published just last week, found that only 14% of SMEs intend to expand overseas while 45% have no plans to internationalise soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Insufficient funding, unfamiliarity with foreign markets, concerns about competition in foreign markets were some of the reasons cited.

sections.label: SGX environmental social governance reporting
sections.summary: SGX made it mandatory for all listed companies to report environmental, social and governance practices from 2018 on a comply or explain basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For instance, the Singapore Exchange (SGX) has made it mandatory for all listed companies to report their environmental, social and governance practices from 2018 onwards on a "comply or explain" basis.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore support for sustainable practices
sections.summary: The passage asks what plans Enterprise Singapore has to support SMEs' adoption of sustainable business practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share what plans Enterprise Singapore has to support SMEs’ adoption of sustainable business practices?

sections.label: Strategies for capacity and expansion
sections.summary: The passage asks what new strategies will assist SMEs in building capacity and remaining relevant in Singapore or expanding abroad.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: What new strategies will be taken to assist them in building capacity and remaining relevant in Singapore, or in expanding their businesses abroad?

sections.label: Redundancies from merger
sections.summary: The passage asks whether there will be redundancies from the merger and what will happen to redundant staff, including redeployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Will there be any redundancies and, if so, what will happen to the staff who are made redundant due to this merger and will they be redeployed?

sections.label: Loan repayment and approved applications
sections.summary: The Member asks how many companies under the schemes owe or cannot repay bank or FI loans, and the number of approved applications under IE Singapore and SPRING Singapore schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Lastly, I would like to know how many companies under the schemes owe or are unable to repay loans from the banks or FIs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask the Minister the number of applications approved under the schemes managed by IE Singapore and SPRING Singapore.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore enterprise-centric approach
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore will adopt an enterprise-centric approach, with programmes accounting for diverse needs and supporting enterprises in all sectors, whether covered by ITMs or not.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, for all these reasons, it is important that our businesses have to adapt, innovate and build new capabilities according to their circumstances, as has been pointed out by several Members in the course of this debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And Enterprise Singapore itself, and I want to again stress this, will adopt an enterprise-centric approach and its programmes will take into account this diversity of needs while rendering support to enterprises in all sectors – to address Mr Thomas Chua's point – regardless of whether they are covered by ITMs or not.

sections.label: Support for micro SMEs and overseas markets
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore will support micro SMEs through TACs, SME Centres and private initiatives, and build on IE Singapore's over 35 overseas centres and trade missions.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And I want to share with Members that SPRING Singapore has already been working with the Federation of Merchants' Associations, Singapore, for example, to drive the growth and transformation of heartland enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, similarly, Enterprise Singapore will continue to support micro SMEs through the TACs and the SME Centres as well as through – and this is important – private sector initiatives, such as the 99% SME campaign which is jointly organised by Singtel and the Development Bank of Singapore (DBS) to drive capability upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore will build on IE Singapore's network of over 35 overseas centres covering regional, developed and emerging markets and it will continue to organise trade missions for our SMEs to explore opportunities in new markets.

sections.label: Support schemes for risks
sections.summary: Economic agencies have sought to mitigate risks through support schemes like the MRA scheme and the GCP scheme for manpower and capability.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Our economic agencies have sought to mitigate some of those risks through support schemes to evaluate the opportunities like the MRA scheme and also to build their manpower and capability, such as the GCP scheme.

sections.label: BGP one-stop grants portal
sections.summary: The BGP was launched in January last year as a one-stop portal for businesses to apply for grants without approaching multiple agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The BGP was launched in January last year to provide a one-stop portal for businesses to apply for grants without having to approach multiple agencies.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore resources and account managers
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore will draw on IE Singapore and SPRING Singapore resources, except consumer protection headcount and budget transferred to CCS, keeping the same account managers where possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore will draw on the combined resources of IE Singapore and SPRING Singapore, except for the headcount and budget that goes with the consumer protection role which will be transferred to CCS.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To ensure business continuity, companies will have the same account managers as far as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I want to stress that because many Members have raised this and it is an important point.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, whether they have been served by SPRING Singapore or by IE Singapore, the commitment is to try and ensure that they have the same account manager.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore preserves SPRING and IE staff
sections.summary: Establishing Enterprise Singapore preserves SPRING and IE Singapore competencies, networks and culture, with officers assured of augmented roles and opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But in establishing Enterprise Singapore, we also have taken care to preserve the competencies, networks and culture that SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore have built over the years.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, I want to assure Members, especially Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Patrick Tay, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Desmond Choo, that all IE Singapore and SPRING Singapore officers can look forward to augmented roles and opportunities and, in some cases, new assignments in Enterprise Singapore.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore leadership appointments
sections.summary: Chairman-designate Peter Ong is former Head of Civil Service and served in MTI; CEO-designate Png Cheong Boon is MTI Second Permanent Secretary.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In terms of leadership, the Chairman-designate, Mr Peter Ong, is the former Head of Civil Service and has also served in MTI.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The CEO-designate, Mr Png Cheong Boon, is the Second Permanent Secretary at MTI and has helmed several economic agencies.

sections.label: SPRING and IE cross-industry funding
sections.summary: In 2017, SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore committed $100 million from FY2016 to FY2020 to encourage impactful cross-industry projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In 2017, SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore committed $100 million from financial year (FY) 2016 to FY2020 to encourage industries to drive impactful cross-industry projects.

sections.label: Enhanced SME Centres and upgrading projects
sections.summary: In 2016 SME Centres were enhanced to provide business diagnosis, run upgrading projects and solve common business challenges, with plans for more group-based projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In 2016, we enhanced our SME Centres to provide business diagnosis, run upgrading projects and solve common business challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: There are also plans for more of such group-based upgrading projects with other SME Centres, TACs and merchant associations so that more of our SMEs can benefit from them.

sections.label: MCI dialogues for Mandarin-speaking SME owners
sections.summary: From October to December last year, MCI, economic agencies and Lianhe Wanbao held dialogues targeting Mandarin-speaking SME owners in sectors like wholesale trade, logistics, retail and F&B.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: From October to December last year, the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) worked with our economic agencies and Lianhe Wanbao to organise a series of dialogues to target the Mandarin-speaking SME business owners in sectors, such as wholesale trade, logistics, retail and F&B.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore combines IE and SPRING resources
sections.summary: Combining IE Singapore and SPRING Singapore under Enterprise Singapore provides holistic support for businesses to develop capabilities, international strategies and partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: By combining the resources and capabilities of IE Singapore and SPRING Singapore under Enterprise Singapore, we will be able to provide holistic support to our businesses to develop deep capabilities, robust international strategies and strong partnerships with stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore will build on the good work that has been done by IE Singapore and SPRING Singapore to grow strong Singapore-based enterprises by helping them to develop deep capabilities and access global opportunities as we make the transition to the next phase of our economic growth.
